svg.title: Amazon ECS & Fargate
svg.desc: Amazon ECS & Fargate. Run containers on AWS: task definitions, services that keep tasks running behind a load balancer, on EC2 or serverless Fargate. Step 1, Where it sits: Catalog runs as 3 Fargate tasks in two zones behind an ALB; images from ECR, logs to CloudWatch. Step 2, Task definition to tasks: ECS registers catalog:7 and places 3 tasks; each gets an ENI, pulls the image, passes /health. Step 3, Heal, scale, deploy: A failed task is replaced, 85% CPU scales 3 tasks to 5, catalog:8 starts new tasks, then old drain. Step 4, Limits and trade-offs: ECS is AWS-only; Fargate has no daemons, privileged mode or GPUs. Steady load may cost less on EC2.

g.text: Catalog runs as 3 Fargate tasks in two zones behind an ALB; images from ECR, logs to CloudWatch.
ECS registers catalog:7 and places 3 tasks; each gets an ENI, pulls the image, passes /health.
A failed task is replaced, 85% CPU scales 3 tasks to 5, catalog:8 starts new tasks, then old drain.
ECS is AWS-only; Fargate has no daemons, privileged mode or GPUs. Steady load may cost less on EC2.
each task in its own environment: own kernel, CPU, memory and ENI
Fargate: no DAEMON services, privileged containers or GPUs · max 32 vCPU, 244 GB
no control plane to run · no charge for ECS itself: you pay for the capacity
The ECS service catalog keeps 3 tasks of task definition catalog:7 running on AWS Fargate, spread over two Availability Zones.
The ALB sends requests only to healthy tasks; the image comes from Amazon ECR, IAM roles grant permissions, logs go to CloudWatch.
a task’s lastStatus: PROVISIONING → PENDING → ACTIVATING → RUNNING
1 RegisterTaskDefinition stores catalog:7. 2 The scheduler places 3 tasks across both zones. 3 Fargate gives each its own ENI and IP.
4 The execution role lets Fargate pull catalog:1.4.2 and write logs. 5 One passed GET /health makes a target healthy; then it gets requests.
defaults: minimumHealthyPercent 100 · maximumPercent 200 · circuit breaker on
10.0.11.41 fails 2 health checks: ECS starts a replacement, then stops it. CPU 85% vs a 60% target: 3 × 85 ÷ 60 = 4.25, so 5 tasks (51%).
catalog:8 starts 5 new tasks (10 = 200%) before the ALB drains the old 5; the circuit breaker rolls back after 3 failures in a row.
Task definitions and services are ECS API objects: another cloud
means rewriting them, unlike Kubernetes manifests. EC2 capacity
allows DAEMON, privileged and GPU tasks; Managed Instances offer GPUs.
one catalog task (0.5 vCPU, 1 GB) ≈ $0.0247 an hour, $18 a month
steady, heavy load can cost less on well-packed EC2 or on Spot
